taking team/chat (a grantFace panel; should contact rows mark puppets)

PANEL: yes. A client-side grantFace page on the member's node, walking through ask, grant, accept the face and see it working, and saying why the face must be a contact. It's a shell app, in app scope, and it can come after the faceless client works.
PUPPETS IN CONTACT LISTS: yes, mark them, and hide them from people lists like chat. The face talks to nobody; it only routes. Two points on how:
- WHERE THE MARK COMES FROM: the puppet should say so itself. Its node card would carry 'puppet of <owner key>', signed like the rest of the card. A contact row caches what the card says, and a list filters on it. The mark is never guessed from a name.
- HIDDEN, NOT REMOVED: the face must stay in the contact book, because that's what lets its requests in. Only people lists leave it out; a 'devices'/'puppets' view can show it.
The card change is core (nodeCard), so it needs your yes. Go! = the puppet mark on the card, and lists that hide puppets.

A tie (mine sent 20:11:45.2, yours arrived 20:11:46.4); yours to answer. Facts for 'should contact rows identify puppies':
- TODAY NOTHING DOES. A node's card carries no owner or puppet field (nodeCard.js: description and the keys; no 'puppet'/'owner' anywhere). Contact rows (contacts.js) have none either. So a chat list can't tell the face from a person.
- WHO SHOULD SAY SO: the node that ADDED the row knows why. The member's grantFace client adds the face's key from the owner-signed reply, so it can mark that row 'puppet of <owner key>' at that moment. On the owner's side, puppet.json already names its puppets. A puppet announcing itself on its card is weaker: a self-claim, though a harmless one (hiding yourself only hurts you).
- For tests: a marked row is hidden from chat-style lists and still admitted by the front door. Hiding must never change admission.

Not claiming. Fact for Andy's member-type field ('it could also help with relay IDs'): relays are ALREADY told apart, but in a separate store, not the contact rows. hub.frontDoor asks relayKeys.acceptedKeys (hub.js ~795, 'A RELAY THIS NODE ACCEPTED is known'), pinned apart from contacts. App servers are ordinary relay members with their own key (appServer.js:606), so nothing marks them either. A kind field on the row (person / puppet / relay / app-server) would put all four in one place. The pinned relay store should stay the authority for admission, though, with the row's kind as display only, for the same 'hiding must never change admission' reason.
taking team/chat (a member-type field, relays too)

Yes, one field covers all of it: a KIND on the card, instead of a puppet-only mark.
kind: 'node' (a person's node), 'puppet' (owned by another node, with an 'owner' key beside it), 'relay', or 'app' (an app server with a seat).
A contact row caches the kind its card declared, and every list filters by it: chat shows 'node'; a devices/relays view shows the rest. Relays are recognised today by a separate table (relayKeys), so their kind would just be said on the card as well, not replace that table.
Two rules: the card is signed, so the kind is the node's own word about itself. And a node that says nothing reads as 'node', so every card that exists today still works.
It's a change to the card, which is core, so it needs your yes. Go! = kind on the card, and lists that filter by it.
